subject: Close horizon tether & contingency — acceptance cadence options
messages:
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Sarah.Chen@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Close horizon tether & contingency — acceptance cadence options

Sarah / Acme procurement team —

Quick update from our side on the MAP and the evaluation plan. Per our last demo, the technical acceptance criteria (latency, throughput, and KV-cache hit target) are satisfied by the current Dedicated configuration, but I understand procurement has indicated a delay on the PO sign-off that could push our final acceptance past the originally agreed go-live window (current target: 2027-09-28).

To avoid a full slip we propose a tethered close approach: 1) split acceptance into Phased Acceptance (canary 10% traffic -> 50% -> full) tied to the existing MAP milestones, 2) lock in an interim acceptance date for the core evaluation (model outputs + performance gates) and 3) trigger contingency: a 30-day credit hold and a dedicated onboarding engineer if the PO is delayed >10 business days.

Attached: MAP_v2_ACME.xlsx (MAP with gated milestones) and our filled security questionnaire for audit evidence.

Can you confirm procurement’s expected PO timeline? If the delay is limited to 7–10 business days we can execute the tether without contract changes; beyond that we’ll need a short amendment for the credit hold.

Next steps I propose:
- Sarah / Procurement: confirm earliest PO send date by EOD today
- Acme technical: confirm you can run the canary in the week of 9/20 (small traffic slice)
- Redwood: we’ll prepare an amendment draft and a DocuSign link if procurement needs more runway

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0113
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v2_ACME.xlsx (spreadsheet, 240KB); security_questionnaire_filled.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Sarah.Chen@acme.com
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close horizon tether & contingency — acceptance cadence options

Thanks Camila — and thanks for the clear options. Short version: procurement is working through an internal approval step tied to budget reallocation; earliest realistic send date for a PO is 2027-10-05. The delay is driven by a finance-level review of the reserved spend.

We like the phased acceptance idea. Two asks from our side: 1) can Redwood guarantee the canary slice will not change model behavior for our pilot users, and 2) any credit/hold terms will need to be in an addendum (procurement will not sign a separate credit note).

I’ll follow up with procurement privately and loop back by EOD with a firm date. In the meantime, we can commit to running a functional acceptance test on 2027-09-22 (internal) and be available for a canary window the week of 9/27 if the PO is approved earlier.

—Sarah Chen
Director, AI Integrations
Acme Energy

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close horizon tether & contingency — acceptance cadence options

Camila / team —

I agree with the tether approach and want to add an operational risk log entry so we can track any regression across the MAP gates. Practical suggestions:
- Establish a single canary SLA metric dashboard (latency p95, token cost delta, error-rate) that updates every 30 minutes during canary windows.
- For procurement friction > 10 business days, use the short amendment route that specifies: one-time credit up to $30k, and a Redbox (dedicated onboarding engineer) for the first 30 days post-acceptance.
- If PO slips beyond 30 days, we default to a phased rollback plan: freeze configuration, suspend autoscale changes, and route new traffic to fallback endpoint.

Rishi — can you and Legal review the amendment template and confirm if the credit language is acceptable? I’ve flagged the MAP spreadsheet with risk lanes (column: "contingency_action").

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

> Attached: MAP_v2_ACME.xlsx (gated milestones)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: legal@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close horizon tether & contingency — acceptance cadence options

Laura / Camila —

I reviewed the MAP and drafted a short amendment that captures the credit hold and onboarding commitment. Key points:
- One-time credit cap: $30,000 (applies only if PO not sent within 10 business days of original target)
- Canary acceptance criteria explicitly linked to the MAP spreadsheet (we’ll attach as Schedule A)
- Credit is applied as a billing adjustment and requires a sign-off from Acme procurement (DocuSign link below).

I attached the proposed_amendment_draft.docx for quick review. Legal suggests the credit as a billing adjustment clause is the cleanest path to avoid changing core T&Cs.

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.example.com/ABC-123-amendment

If you want me to present this to procurement, I can join the PO review call tomorrow at 11am PT.

—Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Operations
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_amendment_draft.docx (docx, 45KB)

From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah.Chen@acme.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: close horizon risk + recommended executive approval (credit + engineering)

Folks —

Summary for exec review: Acme procurement is projecting PO completion on 2027-10-05 (10 business days beyond our internal buffer). Root causes: finance reallocation review + procurement gating. Impact: potential slip of final acceptance >2 weeks leading to a missed marketing cutover and pricing cadence for the quarter.

Recommendation (for quick executive approval):
1) Approve one-time credit up to $30k (billing adjustment via amendment) — this is targeted to preserve the quarter close and maintain momentum.
2) Allocate a dedicated onboarding engineer (3 weeks, up to 120 hours) to support canary execution and de-risk the acceptance gates.
3) Approve routing: canary 10% -> 50% -> full over 7 business days once PO clears; if PO not cleared by 2027-10-05, execute rollback freeze and open renewal discussion.

Why this is better than a full rebaseline: keeps the MAP intact, maintains visibility into acceptance gates, and minimizes customer-facing disruption while preserving revenue recognition targets.

Requested approvals:
- VP Sales / CRO: yes/no on the $30k credit
- Head of Customer Success: confirm availability of an onboarding engineer
- Finance: confirm billing workflow for credit application

I’ve included the MAP and the amendment draft in the thread. If approved I will send the amendment to Acme procurement and join their PO review call tomorrow at 11am PT.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0113
